rationale: fasta is a tiny (2-function, ~1KB text) but compute-kernel-heavy benchmark dominated by a hot loop in main with arithmetic, a probability lookup table (iub), and frequent character output, so the table favors passes that obscure dataflow and control structure cheaply while penalizing heavyweight transformations on the hot path. SUB gets the highest tolerance with low cost weights because arithmetic substitution is nearly free and effective on fasta's integer/float mix; FLA carries the highest SecurityGain weight since flattening main's loop-and-branch structure is the strongest single deterrent for a single-function program, but its RuntimeCost weight is held mid-range to avoid pathological degradation of the inner generation loop; SPLIT is kept cheap to feed FLA more granular blocks; BCF and IBR are moderate — opaque predicates and indirect branches add real per-iteration cost on a hot loop, so their cost weights temper application frequency; IGV is moderately weighted to obscure the nucleotide/probability tables that a reverse engineer would immediately recognize, with low size cost given the tiny data section; ICALL is omitted entirely because fasta makes almost no direct calls, so indirect-call rewriting would add overhead with negligible security return in a 2-function binary.
